about.title: Cotati Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Cotati is a small city, but defective products don't respect city limits — a faulty appliance bought online, a malfunctioning power tool used on Old Redwood Highway job sites, or a poorly labeled household chemical can injure someone just as easily here as in a larger county seat. Under California law, product liability claims often rest on strict liability: you generally don't need to prove the manufacturer was careless, only that the product had a design, manufacturing, or warning defect and that defect caused harm. That standard can apply whether the responsible party is the original maker, a distributor, or the retailer who sold it. If a defective product hurt you or someone in your household near Cotati, keeping the item exactly as it was at the time of injury matters. Our team can evaluate what happened and explain your options.

whyChoose.title: Why Strict Liability Matters for Your Claim

items.title: You Don't Have to Prove Negligence
items.desc: Because California generally applies strict liability to defective products, you typically need to show the product was defective and caused your injury — not that anyone acted carelessly.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, which gives our team several avenues to pursue on your behalf.

items.title: Preserving the Product Preserves Your Case
items.desc: Keeping the defective item intact, along with packaging and receipts, helps us build a stronger case around the specific defect that caused harm.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not usually. California product liability claims often rely on strict liability, meaning you generally need to show the product itself was defective and that the defect caused your injury. This can make it possible to hold a manufacturer, distributor, or retailer responsible without proving carelessness.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Keep it exactly as it was at the time of the injury, including any packaging, instructions, or receipts. Don't attempt repairs or modifications, since the product itself is often the most important piece of evidence in these claims.
